relationship_to_primary.primary_question: Is trait variance larger than family variance, or vice versa?
relationship_to_primary.primary_hold_reason: The 201-edge graph recovered the sign of a twofold variance contrast but failed the predeclared MAE<=0.35 magnitude-recovery criterion.
relationship_to_primary.new_question_independent: Does trait identity and/or family identity contribute a reproducible nonzero component of phylogenetic memory loss, without ranking the two components?

biological_hypotheses.trait_repeatability: The same trait carries some repeatable memory-loss tendency across independent families.
biological_hypotheses.lineage_repeatability: The same family carries some repeatable memory-loss tendency across multiple traits.
biological_hypotheses.both: Both crossed identities contribute repeatable structure.
biological_hypotheses.neither: Observed family x trait heterogeneity is not recoverably structured by either crossed identity at this graph size.

graph.source: frozen final crossed core from workflow run 37086693588 artifact 11263253304

calibration_and_admission.null_calibration: For each component, set a one-sided 95th-percentile detection threshold from its estimated variance under the null benchmark.
calibration_and_admission.rule: PASS only if null-calibrated power is >=0.80 for the corresponding 0.005 component on both axes and >=90% fits are valid. Do not compare component magnitudes.

if_pass.real_effect_question: Fit the frozen crossed model to real rho and report whether each variance component exceeds its independently calibrated null threshold; do not classify trait-dominant versus lineage-dominant.
if_pass.multiplicity: The two component-presence decisions are co-primary and use separate pre-calibrated 5% null thresholds; report both without selecting the more favorable axis.

if_hold: Stop before opening real rho. Do not lower component size or power requirement.

boundary_handling.singular_fit: Not invalid for this component-presence problem. Boundary estimates are expected under null or one-component benchmarks.
boundary_handling.variance_extraction: Extract nonnegative REML variance components from VarCorr even when isSingular=TRUE.
boundary_handling.invalid_fit: Only optimizer/model errors or nonfinite variance extraction count invalid.
boundary_handling.reason: Testing presence of a variance component is intrinsically a boundary problem; discarding singular fits would condition away the null.
